verdict_basis: the frozen bar's own check_order, applied in order; all five checks confirmed
why_this_artifact_exists: Link 4 completed on 2026-11-16 and was never retrieved, so no verdict had ever been computed. Retrieval and interpretation are kept as two reviewable steps: the raw result is wiki/finetune_arm_session4_2026-11-16.json, committed untouched, and this file is the reading of it.

check_order_applied.evidence: EXECUTED, not argued. scripts/finetune_arm_run.py:56 IMPORTS the incumbent's own split function (leave_peak_out_indices from scripts.positional_arm_score) rather than reimplementing it, and line 505 READS split_frac from the bar's comparator record (0.25) rather than choosing one. Re-running leave_peak_out_indices(tiles, frac=0.25, seed=s) over the 44,106-tile cohort reproduces the recorded n_train for 10 of 10 seeds exactly: 32908, 33088, 32733, 33223, 33081, 33199, 33516, 32857, 33445, 33416.
check_order_applied.distinct_property_also_recorded_by_the_r: peaks_shared_between_splits = 0 on all 10 seeds. That is a LEAKAGE check, a different property from split equality, and it is named separately here so the two are not conflated.
check_order_applied.why_it_needed_checking: The bar's comparator says the comparison is against the frozen encoder on BYTE-IDENTICAL splits, because identical splits are what make the difference attributable to the representation rather than to the data partition. The incumbent also carries recomputed_in_run=false, so it is a carried-forward constant -- which is exactly the case where split drift would go unnoticed.

check_order_applied.evidence: the gate is: max|null| must fall below 0.50 x the arm's own measured signal. max|null| 0.1997 < 0.50 x 0.6405 = 0.3203
check_order_applied.a_correction_recorded_rather_than_hidden: first read as a FAILURE and retracted within one message. The gate is a RATIO, not an absolute; 0.1997 looks large beside the 0.05-style absolute bars elsewhere in this project and is comfortably inside half the measured signal.

check_order_applied.evidence: median 0.6405 against the committed incumbent 0.5076 = +0.1329, against an inherited margin of 0.02 (6.6x the requirement)
check_order_applied.multiplicity: exactly ONE comparison is declared by the bar, so no correction applies; the bar records that contrast deliberately.

against_the_ceiling.note: uses the cross-frame ceiling normalization added on 2026-11-17 -- each score read against its own frame's ceiling rather than against a bare threshold
against_the_ceiling.reading: fine-tuning takes the fraction of achievable signal from 34.4% to 68.1%, roughly doubling it. That is precisely the revival condition the G-A scope note names: a candidate that raises fraction_of_ceiling, rather than one that merely widens a margin over a collapsing comparator.

honest_limits: THE HORIZON DEVIATED FROM THE BAR, AND THIS IS THE REAL LIMIT. The bar states a 38-epoch diagnostic horizon; the run executed 7. The run RECORDS the deviation and argues it cannot move the verdict, because the verdict reads only the frozen 7-epoch prefix while the horizon governs the pre-declared INELIGIBLE tail. That argument is sound for the verdict. But the 38-epoch tail existed specifically to close the question would more budget have helped EMPIRICALLY, and that question is therefore NOT closed. This is a frozen-budget result, not a converged one.

The null clears the ratio gate but is NOT the benign case. The run's own how_to_read_a_HIGH_null field says a null that merely MATCHES the untrained baseline says nothing about the fine-tune; these nulls sit about 0.29 ABOVE an untrained baseline that is negative (-0.1123, -0.0481, -0.1530). Training on destroyed labels still reaches about 0.18 where an untrained encoder reaches about -0.11. The gate passes; that margin over the untrained baseline is worth carrying forward rather than filing as clean.

3 null replicates is enough to show the fit collapses when the labels are destroyed, which is the claim. It is NOT enough to estimate a null distribution. That scope limit is the run's own wording, kept verbatim.

One substrate (GSE144621 peak tiles), one rung, one encoder, one comparison. Nothing here speaks to other substrates, and nothing here addresses the GENERATIVE question the project's north star names -- this is a discriminative scoring result.

The 277 MB of trained checkpoints are deliberately NOT in this repository, because the standing rule keeps heavy files off C:. They exist as the pa-finetune-chain-s4 kernel output on Kaggle: 13 .pt files of 22,305,931 bytes each (seed_0 through seed_9, null_0 through null_2). Their small per-epoch curve JSONs ARE committed beside this file.
